title: Same Tree
corePattern: Synchronous Tree Traversal - Simultaneous DFS/BFS Comparison
interviewTips: Ask clarifier: Are empty trees (both null) considered same? Yes. What defines sameness - both structure and values must match exactly?
Trade-off: Recursive DFS is shortest to write but uses O(h) call stack and can overflow on skewed tree of 10^4+ depth; iterative BFS/DFS uses explicit queue/stack and is safer for production.

Edge-case tip: Check nulls before accessing val to avoid NPE; check both structure mismatch (one null, one not) and value mismatch separately; test [1,2] vs [1,null,2] which looks similar but structure differs.

approaches.name: Approach 1: Recursive DFS (Preorder Comparison)
approaches.intuition: Two trees are same if roots have same value and left subtrees are same and right subtrees are same. This is naturally recursive: compare pair (p,q), then recurse on (p.left,q.left) and (p.right,q.right). Base cases handle nulls.
approaches.theory: This is a synchronous preorder traversal of both trees. At each pair we enforce three invariants: 1) both null -> true, 2) exactly one null -> false (structure differs), 3) values differ -> false. Otherwise the answer is conjunction of left and right results. It visits each node pair at most once, short-circuits on first mismatch via &&.

timeComplexity.explanation: Each node pair visited once where n is min number of nodes, worst-case total nodes in both trees. Early exit on mismatch gives O(k) best case.

spaceComplexity.explanation: Recursion call stack depth equals tree height h. O(log n) for balanced, O(n) for skewed chain. No extra data structure.

steps: recurse left: compare (2,2): vals equal 2==2, both leaves -> true
recurse right: compare (3,3): vals equal 3==3, both leaves -> true

edgeCases: Same values different structure: p=[1,2], q=[1,null,2] -> false
Same structure different values: p=[1,2,1], q=[1,1,2] -> false
Skewed chain depth 10000: recursion may overflow in some languages

approaches.name: Approach 2: Iterative BFS with Queue
approaches.intuition: Process both trees level by level in lockstep. Keep a queue of pairs (a,b) to compare. Pop a pair, apply same null/value checks as recursion, then enqueue (a.left,b.left) and (a.right,b.right). If queue drains with no mismatch, trees are identical.
approaches.theory: This is synchronous breadth-first traversal. Pairing nodes guarantees structural alignment is checked explicitly, including null placeholders. Unlike recursion it uses heap-allocated queue, avoiding call-stack overflow. Order can be BFS (queue) or DFS (stack) - correctness is identical because all pairs must match regardless of order. Short-circuits immediately on first structural or value mismatch.

timeComplexity.explanation: Each pair dequeued and compared once. n is total nodes visited. O(n) worst case, early exit on mismatch.

spaceComplexity.explanation: Queue holds at most one full level (width w). Worst O(n) for complete tree last level ~n/2, best O(1) for skewed chain. No recursion stack.

steps: pop (2,null): one null one not -> return false

edgeCases: Both null: queue starts [(null,null)] -> continue -> true
Single node same: p=[1], q=[1] -> true
Single node diff val: p=[1], q=[2] -> false
Asymmetric nulls at depth: p=[1,2,3], q=[1,2,null] -> false on (3,null) pair
Large balanced tree: queue memory ~ O(n/2) at last level, acceptable
